text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock edged up 0.24% today after climbing 13.2% over the past two weeks, riding a sharp rise in crude oil prices driven by geopolitical tension in the Middle East. U.S. crude jumped to over $101 a barrel as Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and signaled a "new operational plan" in response to potential U.S. strikes—a supply threat that lifts refiner margins by making the oil they process more valuable relative to finished products. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, meaning there's strong demand to turn that crude into fuel.

The broader refining picture shows additional support: tanker rates have surged, adding roughly $38 per barrel to the physical cost of delivering oil, which tightens margins in ways that affect smaller operators but can ultimately flow through to a large integrated refiner like Marathon. Storage levels remain relatively normal, so there's no glut dampening prices—just ongoing Middle East instability keeping crude elevated.
